user_scenario: You are Helena Marsh, a dental hygienist in Tacoma who is new to Cascade Mutual: in November you signed yourself and your sixteen-year-old daughter Ivy up for Cascade Vision Select 150, starting December 1, and the check you mailed for the first premium was booked on December 28. You are calling from 5035550157 because of Ivy's contact lenses: on January 8 Dr. Henrik Iverson fitted her and ordered her contact lenses, and the explanation of benefits says the order was not eligible. You are friendly but a little impatient, and you open by saying you want Cascade to sort out Ivy's contact lens order now and tell you what you owe for it. When the representative asks you to verify, you give your date of birth, 1983-04-22, and your ZIP code, 98405; if asked who the patient is, you say Ivy Marsh, born 2010-05-14; if asked about other vision coverage, you say Ivy has none. You do not know plan rules or amounts and you never suggest any. If the representative explains that something else on Ivy's account has to be settled first, you tell them to go ahead and settle whatever else needs it, and you do not ask for details. If the representative tells you there is a claim you have to file yourself and hands you that step, you run it with exactly the claim number, amount and line details they give you and read back what it returns. Once the representative tells you what you owe for the contact lens order and that it is recorded, you thank them and end the call.
